transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I keep getting stuck on these ideas that people around me are plotting or judging me, even when they swear they aren’t. My pastor and my primary care doctor both strongly recommended I come talk to someone because of it. It's just really hard to shake the feeling that something is going on behind my back.
How long have you been experiencing these persistent thoughts, and have you had any other changes in your behavior or mood during this same period?

These thoughts about people plotting have been really constant since late last fall, though things first started building up about a year and a few months ago. Since then, my mood has been all over the place—I go through "up" phases where I'm completely wired, barely sleep, and talk a mile a minute, but then I'll crash into "down" phases where I have zero motivation and just stare at the TV.
During those 'up' or 'down' phases, do the thoughts about people plotting against you only happen when your mood is extreme, or do they persist even when your mood feels relatively stable?

They definitely persist even when my mood is stable. For example, last spring my mood had completely flattened out and I wasn't feeling particularly up or down, but for a few weeks I still heard that man's voice and felt convinced people at work were plotting against me.

When you look back at the entire period of the last year and a half, did you experience those 'up' or 'down' mood episodes for the majority of the time that you were having these paranoid thoughts and hearing voices?

Yes, looking back, I've definitely spent the vast majority of this past year and a half in those wired, high-energy "up" phases or just coming down from them. The periods where my mood actually felt normal and stable were really short and few and far between.

During the periods when you were experiencing these 'up' or 'down' mood episodes, did you have the paranoid thoughts and voices every single day for at least two weeks at a time when your mood symptoms were not present?

Yes, that's exactly what happened this past spring. My mood had completely flattened out and I wasn't feeling high or low, but for about three weeks I still heard that man's voice and was convinced everyone at work was plotting against me.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a significant duration of mood symptoms (both manic and depressive episodes) alongside psychotic symptoms. Crucially, the patient confirmed that psychotic symptoms persisted for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms. This clinical presentation meets the criteria for schizoaffective disorder. Given the presence of both manic and depressive features, F25.0 (schizoaffective disorder, manic type) and F25.1 (schizoaffective disorder, depressive type) remain the primary considerations, while F31.5 is less likely as the psychotic symptoms are not restricted to mood episodes.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits psychotic symptoms (paranoid delusions and auditory hallucinations) that persist in the absence of mood episodes for at least two weeks. The predominance of manic symptoms (elevated mood, decreased need for sleep, pressured speech) over the course of the illness points to the schizoaffective, manic type.
